entries.title: The test-manifest check fails on missing, unknown, uncovered and duplicate IDs, untagged skipped tests, .only and stray test files
The generated-file freshness check finds missing, changed and extra files

No file in the repository names a machine's role, a path under a real home or an OS build number, also when the phrase is split over a comment's lines, while product language about a Linux desktop and fixture homes pass
Every dependency rule fires on a fixture tree with violations, and tests are exempt only from the production layering rules
The custom lint rules refuse os.tmpdir(), shell: true, .cmd spawns, exec and execSync through any binding, AppData paths in package code, and stdout writes, console and dynamic loads in the bridge
pnpm verify runs the serial lab tests on --lab, TASKS_VERIFY_LAB=1, an unknown base or a change to lab or shared files, and otherwise says it skipped them
Product names live in one place: TT Tasks, Tasks inside the app, by TumbleToad; the CLI name and the environment prefix derive from the identifier, the MCP key is a plain identifier of its own

The M0 spike kit self-test: handshake and its deadlines, MCP envelopes of both eras, forwarder, page, token, WebSocket and Reveal, shim and run shim, probe redaction, owner-only permissions, socket folder, scratch tree, bench

The M0 spike page (U rows) builds with Vite and loads under the strict CSP: fresh style nonce in header and meta, no inline script or style, same-origin assets with matching integrity hashes, WOFF2 fonts from the origin within budget, no service worker file, the runner's result files hold no token

The M0.07 lifecycle lab: the forwarder reconnects and replays initialize, also one sent during a slow handshake, the service's environment snapshot, its parsers and E01's differences, the tasksw.exe supervisor stand-in, the lab release folder and its entry

Lab session 3's cold-start timers count an answer only when the expected service gave it, check both replies by their JSON structure after the clock stops (a malformed reply, the right fragments in the wrong structure, a wrong id or a notification never count), reject a stale service.json and a process of the install's runtime with another entry, and stop every process they start, also at a hung bridge, a failure or a signal; E01 stops the Windows supervisor and service when it fails
The storage bench runs its generators and R02 to R06 at 1 % scale and writes complete result files
The storage bench's fixture generator gives the same corpus for the same seed
A failed storage bench run closes its connections, removes its run folder and reports the original error, with the removal error when that fails too
A storage bench row gives a verdict only when the run meets its prescribed scale, counts and durations, and is indicative otherwise
The storage bench's timed writes use random A1 IDs and agent sessions, and its projection rebuild records projection_files and acknowledges the outbox
Packaging spike: the runtime gate passes on the pinned Node 26.13.1 with SQLite 3.54.1 and fails when a check fails
Packaging spike: the Node download must match SHASUMS256.txt, its gpgv-verified signature and the pinned digest
Packaging spike: the version folder layout, its manifest and reproducible tar.gz and zip archives
Packaging spike: the POSIX and C launchers pass hostile argv to Node byte for byte and remove NODE_OPTIONS
Packaging spike: install.sh and install.ps1 verify the SHA256SUMS signature and the archive hash before anything from the archive runs
M0.05 lab checks: the sync detector on fixture trees, owner-only modes and ACLs in a temporary folder, and the identifier and Smart App Control classifiers

The M0.09 lab code: a child of the clean spawner sees no agent variables, the probe records names, matches and ID formats but no values, the key-level recorder compares every named file and proves exact removal through a fake CLI, the removal rule refuses anything not strictly inside the run scratch folder, no CLI output reaches the lab logs or files, and every child ends through one cleanup path

The M0.10 lab code: the text-level trust-entry patch for Claude Code's .claude.json and Codex's config.toml, and its undo, restore every fixture file byte for byte by the config recorder (no file, no projects, other entries, comments and odd whitespace, CRLF and LF, a byte order mark, an existing entry with another value); a file changed after the patch reverts only Tasks's key, and only while it still holds Tasks's value; unsupported layouts and files the scanner cannot account for are refused untouched; the lab command refuses a scratch folder it did not create

The M0.11 lab code through fake CLIs: the recorder keeps the raw stream in its folder with exit code, line structure and schema event keys, refuses agent variables, leaves through one cleanup path (also for a missing executable), cancels by console event, taskkill or signal and sweeps what is left by PID, name and start time; the console helper refuses an unreadable process list; the sanitiser gives every allow-listed field one treatment whatever the input (the reviewer's adversarial values, wrong types, e-mail keys), names unknown fields by placeholders and publishes all or nothing after the checks; the lab refuses Windows-only commands and full access off Windows, and keeps CLI stderr, errors and events with private values out of its console, results and fixtures

The committed stream fixtures pass the content check: the decoded keys and values of every line hold no user or host name, home path, e-mail address, token or key shape, IPv4 or IPv6 address or machine name from a deny-list built at run time; every value is one its schema treatment can produce, every inventory path and index field is a schema name or placeholder, every fixture line is JSON except the one cut final line, and a truncated fixture is its source cut

The claude driver against a fake Claude Code that speaks exactly the recorded print-mode exchanges: the request is the program's first line of input and never an argument, the result's answer and verdict are the work's, the permission maps to Claude Code's own modes, a command and a call of Tasks' tools report their progress, a permission prompt is declined and counted, a question for the person ends the run as needing the person with the question kept and a later one changes nothing, an unknown request gets the protocol's error, a signed-out program ends with its own words and the sign-in command, background work keeps the input open until the program's own turn about it, Stop between turns, during the turn, during start-up and of a silent program, a program that does not exit after its work settles with its answer, a program that stops writing, and a whole answer after megabytes of other output

tasks run with a Claude Code instance: the request reaches the agent on its input and on no process's command line, the run's tools are a private file in the run's folder with the only Tasks entry and a ticket no command line carries, the agent's calls through it bind to the run's session and are recorded with the run's ID, its entry opens nothing once the run ended, the request, the answer and the ticket are in no file of the state folder but the run's own, a person with more than one instance names one, Stop cancels a Claude Code run during its turn, and a signed-out Claude Code ends the run with the command to sign in

A Claude Code run in the run host with real processes, behind its npm shim, in a job object on Windows and without a process group everywhere: start to answer with the request on the program's input and on no command line, Stop during a turn and during start-up over the program's input, a program that does not exit after its work is ended with its answer kept, a process the agent left behind is ended and the cleanup says so, and nothing of a run is left alive

The recorded Claude Code print-mode exchanges hold only what their sanitiser writes (protocol words, built-in tool names, synthetic IDs, fixture paths, names, times, texts and numbers) and pass the stream fixtures' scan; the sanitiser drops a recording's paths, servers, skills, models, prompts and answers, and the check refuses any other value

The recorded codex app-server exchanges hold only what their sanitiser writes (protocol words, synthetic IDs, fixture paths, texts and numbers) and pass the stream fixtures' scan; the sanitiser drops a recording's paths, account, machine name, prompts, answers and ticket, and the check refuses any other value
The M0 bridge harness runs B01 to B07 at a tiny size, reads process memory from outside, writes a result file per row and judges none of them
The M0 bridge harness stops every forwarder and service process it started when a row fails: a memory reading, the service start or the direct client
The registry lint rejects a field without .describe() or with a description over 80 characters
The registry check rejects every other schema, metadata, operation, naming, budget, CLI and example rule on a failing fixture entry
Zod and Ajv give the same verdict on every example and its mutations, and at the boundaries of every field, used by an example or not

Values fuzzed from each JSON Schema: Zod and Ajv agree, parseInput returns a value its schema accepts again unchanged, the agent input stays within the full input, every agent rule and default in the entry data takes effect, and every schema the registry check accepts, hostile probes included, holds all of these
Every generated JSON Schema is valid draft 2020-12, every entry's metadata is consistent and every result can express what its input asks for
The generated files match a fresh render and are byte-stable: LF, sorted keys, no timestamps, no absolute paths

Every verb whose contract says the command line fills base reads one for each of its writes by a read that writes nothing: the task it names or the bound task, or a read action of its own entry; a create needs none

The agent input built from an entry's rules drops hidden fields, requires the required ones and applies the agent limits by path, and mcp-tools.json lists only agent entries with an MCP face; the tools that create a task ask for an effort estimate on the default scale
SafeText strips tag, bidirectional, control and zero-width characters and normalises to NFC with LF; limits count code points and hold on the normalised text
The generated client posts to the generated routes and throws AppError on an error envelope

Driver contract suite: open, busy timeout first and A1's pragma order, statements, transactions, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, typed errors, close, missing and corrupt files, single-step backup into a new file only, and no ATTACH or VACUUM INTO of a named file
The start-up check asks the driver for its own SQLite, and a simulated build without FTS5, or with an old version, no JSON, no STRICT or no backup API, refuses to open
Connections in storage worker threads: the typed protocol, and a writer and two readers that start together open cleanly in repeated rounds

Schema lint on a freshly created space: every table STRICT, no forbidden column names, primary keys, the WITHOUT ROWID rule, ID and instant types, version maps, resolvable foreign keys, enum and JSON CHECKs that match the code and refuse bad values
ID property test: a typed prefix and 26 Crockford base32 characters that encode exactly the 128 bits of the OS random source, with one spelling per ID and strict validation

Short references: task references and entry ordinals format and parse as the contracts patterns do, the default prefix avoids taken ones, and allocation inside a transaction never reuses and stops at its range
Through the service, a change made at the command line is undone from the page after the service restarted, and redone at the command line: the undo history is the space's, shared by every client
Through the service, a claim of a restored copy goes on from its original's task references, and a restore in place goes on from the claimed copy's

Over random sequences of creates, backups and restores in place, no task reference is given to a second task; a backup from a later state keeps its counter, and a live space that does not open still lends its own

Create and open a space folder: space.json, schema 0.1, epoch 1 and a random incarnation, owner-only modes; refusals for an existing or missing folder, another database, a newer, unknown or inconsistent revision and a mismatched space_id, each leaving the database's bytes and journal mode as they were; a rollback journal or an empty database file refused before SQLite opens it; a change between inspection and the writer refused before any persistent pragma, and before the first read when the file system shows it; space.json rebuilt by the writer only when it is missing or stale

space.json's safety fields (space_id, format, min_reader, min_writer) are each read on their own and honoured whatever else is damaged; a damaged manifest (not a JSON object, too large, no marker, a safety field missing or invalid) makes the writer refuse and is never rewritten, and a reader reads on; app versions compare by SemVer precedence

An atomic file write writes every byte through short writes, removes its temporary file on any failure and throws the first error; a failing cleanup never replaces it, and no error carries a path or a native message
Space path rules: absolute, a portable slug as the folder name, and on Windows no trailing dot or space, reserved character or device name in any component
Row decoders refuse a bigint, a fraction, a wrong type or a value outside the guarded integer ranges, which match the contracts wire patterns
A backup taken under 10 writers restores into a new folder with a passing integrity_check, and last_seq and the counts equal the sidecar's; the snapshot is transactionally consistent

A backup is a single-step copy from a read-only connection, checked with integrity_check, compressed and read back, with a sidecar of the snapshot's facts and owner-only files under A1's name, reserved so that two backups never share or replace one name, in a backups folder synced into its parent when new
A crash at each point of a backup leaves either a complete backup or leftovers that are never listed as one, and the space untouched; a failure removes everything the backup wrote

Listing a space's backups: complete ones newest first, a missing or resized data file and an invalid sidecar by state, crash leftovers named and removable, only a backup's own files ever removed and only once untouched for an hour, sidecars found by path as a restore finds them, out-of-range names ignored

The shared BundlePolicy on .db.gz files: a highly compressible space round-trips; a database over the limit is refused before a backup writes and while a restore streams, leaving no folder; free disk space is checked

Daily backups are due after 03:00 local time or at start after 24 hours, a future-dated one aside; retention of one space's backups keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly, pre-migration backups for 30 days, manual ones, the newest complete backup, and never the newest that passes every check a restore makes; it removes only the regular files it listed

A backup publishes its data and its sidecar by a hard link or an exclusive create, never a rename: a pair or a part of one planted under its names while it runs is never replaced, its own files go, and without hard links the copies restore

Verified means a trial restore: a backup whose every check passes but whose restore fails at its first write (the read-only mark) is not verified, retention keeps the older backup that restores instead of removing it, a restore refuses the backup with BACKUP_INVALID and restore latest goes past it; the trials leave no file beside the backups

A reader opens both files of a backup before it reads either and reads only through them: retention removing a backup while its verification holds both files leaves the verification passing, and a restore whose files are removed after they are open restores the backup whole

The backup writer and the exporter check the shared free-space reserve against their estimated peak before they write anything: one byte short is BUNDLE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with no backups or exports folder made, exactly enough runs

Rotation removes only what A1's retention allows: a property test over random backup sets, clocks and offsets never removes a manual backup, the newest complete one, a pre-migration one under 30 days, another space's or a damaged one; on real files manual backups, the newest verified one and a damaged newer one stay

A restore refuses an archive with `..`, an absolute or drive path, a backslash, empty or dot parts, device names or NFD, a link, device or FIFO by its attributes, a Windows reparse point, too many entries, too many expanded bytes declared or produced, an oversized file, duplicate names by case, a file where a folder is, overlapping entries, encryption, another method, an unknown or unlisted file, a wrong checksum or no archive at all, and leaves no folder

Export bundles in backup, fork and transfer mode hold the vacuumed snapshot, space.json, export.json, the live attachments' blobs and data.jsonl when asked, owner-only under A1's name; they restore as read-only copies; a changed bundle is refused; a fault before publication leaves nothing, after it the bundle stays; publication never replaces a file at its name, with or without hard links

The export's secret scan: an export that finds nothing writes its bundle; a secret-shaped string in any table, with or without data.jsonl, or in an attachment is a warning on the written bundle that names each kind and place once but never the text; the vacuumed snapshot holds no byte of text edited away; an attachment reached through a link into the secrets folder is refused

The largest stress-corpus bundle passes the shared BundlePolicy: 10,000 open and 100,000 completed tasks export with data.jsonl and restore with the same counts, and a projection-sized archive of 110,001 files reads under the policy through ZIP64's end records

The restore drill: a backup and an export bundle each restore into a new folder with a passing integrity_check and the live space's last_seq and counts, open read-only, and so does a copy of the restored folder; restored in place from the bundle the space is claimed with a new epoch and its old folder kept

entries.title: The two actions for a failed check through the CLI: restore latest restores the space's newest backup that verifies into a new folder as a read-only copy, skipping and keeping a newer one that does not; rescue writes every readable row into exchange/rescued; the read-only words name both and never a new backup

Rescue of a damaged database keeps the rows that can still be read from a private copy of its files: a table that fails partway is named by its product name, the others are written whole, every file of the space folder stays byte for byte (a write-ahead log beside an empty database, one with rows not checkpointed, a hot journal), a table the product does not have is neither written nor named, and each rescue writes a new file of its own

The secret patterns of A6 3.16.4 find each kind of token alone and inside text, and across a chunk boundary through the kept overlap, and leave ordinary words, short or digitless look-alikes and public keys unflagged
A migration whose barrier backup fails, at any point, never starts; a write between the backup and the migration stops it too; the space then opens read-only with the reason
A failed daily backup, or a newest backup that does not restore, is shown by doctor and the space list with its cause and what to run, through a running service, and goes when a backup succeeds again

A migration starts only behind a barrier backup that passes a trial restore: one that reads back but does not restore, or a full disk at the trial restore, stops it, and the space stays readable at its revision

The migration runner from 0.1 through the real 0.2 and 0.3 and a stand-in 0.4: one system commit per step, user_version, format, undo floor and space.json; a step that fails midway, in its verify or on a foreign key leaves the space at its revision, and it still opens

The 0.1 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.1 chain, with the 0.1 builds' digest) migrates to the build's latest revision behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.1 row stays, one migration commit per step, the new tables empty but the search index, which holds the tasks, the schema equal to a new space's and to the pinned released schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture's counts, last_seq and rows

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.1 to 0.2 migration (the 0.2 chain), one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the fixture's, it opens read-only with A1's message, the 0.1 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

An older build refuses to open a 0.2 space writable: the 0.1 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.2 backup

The 0.2 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.2 chain, with a row in every 0.2 table) migrates to 0.3 behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.2 row stays, one migration commit, the sessions and runs tables empty, the schema equal to a new 0.3 space's and to the pinned 0.3 schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture's counts, last_seq and rows

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.2 to 0.3 migration, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.2 fixture's, it opens read-only with A1's message, the 0.2 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.2 build refuses to open a 0.3 space writable: the 0.2 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.3 backup

The 0.3 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.3 chain, with a session row) migrates to 0.4 behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.3 row stays, one migration commit, the search index equal to a rebuild with every document kind and finding a task by a word of its title, the schema equal to a new 0.4 space's and to the pinned 0.4 schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.3 to 0.4 migration, the search index's fill included, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.3 sample's, it opens read-only with the failure's message, the 0.3 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.3 build refuses to open a 0.4 space writable: the 0.3 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.4 backup

The 0.4 fixture (the Mira sample built by the 0.4 chain, with its project's place row and a session row) migrates to 0.5 behind its verified barrier backup: every 0.4 row stays, the place rows and their history read as before, one migration commit, an empty folders table, the same search documents, the schema equal to a new 0.5 space's and to the pinned 0.5 schema, and the barrier backup restores the fixture

A fault at every statement boundary of the 0.4 to 0.5 migration, one at a time, and a COMMIT that SQLite refuses, roll it back: the space's database, its schema and space.json are the 0.4 sample's, it opens read-only with the failure's message, the 0.4 build still writes it, and without the fault it migrates

A 0.4 build refuses to open a 0.5 space writable: the 0.4 chain's writer, in the calling thread and in its storage worker, is refused with SPACE_TOO_NEW and changes nothing, its reader reads, and it restores no 0.5 backup

Areas and projects through the write path: create with a slug from the title, numbered when taken, in one request with a task filed into the new project; rename and other fields with a base, keeping the ID, slug and tasks; a project moved to another area with all its tasks, its undo a conflict when a task was filed into it since; archive and unarchive, idempotent, keeping the group's tasks as they are; delete refused while a project holds tasks, delete and restore of an empty one; undo and redo of each, and an undo of a create kept by another's task

Folders through the write path: a project created with its folder in one commit and one undo step, the path stored exactly as sent; a moved folder, with a base, carrying every folder inside it, other projects' and their tasks' too, in one undo step, a task's moved folder carrying a project's inside it, and a change without carry changing the owner's folder alone; a move refused whole when it would land a project inside it on another live project's folder; FOLDER_TAKEN for a second live project on one folder, nested folders allowed; a project's delete removing its folders on every machine and its restore bringing them back but one another project took, named in the result; an undo that meets a taken folder is a conflict and its partial form brings the project back without it; a folder changed to one inside or around the old one moves no task folder, a deleted task's moves with a real move; a stale base meets a folder the move would carry or a folder cleared since as a conflict; a deleted project never holds a live folder or task, through undo, redo, a task's restore or several operations of one request; one request changes an owner's folder once; a task's folder set, changed and cleared; paths the request's machine cannot name refused

Property tests over random folder sets and clears, task moves, deletes and restores, project moves, deletes and restores, undos and redos on a Linux and a Windows machine, with an agent's changes between: one live folder per owner and machine, never two live projects on one folder by the machine's case rule, a deleted project holds no live folder or task and a task is in its project's area, a project's or a task's moved folder carries exactly every other folder inside the old one on that machine, and a change without carry the owner's folder alone, by an oracle of the test's own, an undo applied whole gives back the space as it was and its redo the space the commit left, and the history invariants hold

A folder's form on each OS (a ~ path, an absolute path, a drive or a share, no empty, . or .. segment, no trailing separator, at most 4,096 characters, no control character or lone surrogate), the case rule (Windows and macOS without case, Linux with) and where a folder lands when its parent moves, by whole segments
The folder a launch uses on a machine: the task's own folder there, else its project's folder there, else the machine where the task's or its project's folder is, else none

A folder's stored form on Linux, macOS and Windows: the home written as ~ by whole segments with the OS's case rule, separators made plain, an upper-case drive, a share, the Unicode form kept, and a relative, drive-relative or .. path refused

The project a working folder belongs to: the deepest project folder that holds it, by whole names and the machine's case rule, exact when it is the project's folder, none for a sibling with a longer name; a project folder reached through a link holds the folders of its target

The marker in a project's or a task's folder: the owners' IDs and an ignore file, no task text; a launch's look finds its own marker, another owner's or another space's, a marker gone after it was written, a marker that cannot be read; an old folder without one is marked quietly; what was marked outlives a restart; a folder that takes no marker opens as before; a clear takes the owner off and the last one the marker; a folder moved with another keeps its marker; a checkout's git status stays clean

The repository a project's folder holds, by name, from the folder's own Git configuration: origin's or the first remote's, none for no remote, a local remote or a folder that is not a checkout, the name alone for an address with a token, and none when the configuration does not answer in time

Folders through the request path of a running service: a project made for a folder in one change, named after its folder when no name is given; the folder moved on disk with a task's folder and another project's inside it moving along, undone and redone in one step each; a folder given another while it is still there leaving the folders inside it, named in the answer; the repository's name in the project list without its address; a folder another project has answered as that project or refused naming it, a project's folder cleared; a folder inside the Tasks home or a space folder, a missing folder, a file and a relative path refused with nothing written; a retry that replays after the project was renamed; a new project named by several drafts or by calls at once made once; an agent's task filed into an area and project it names first, created with it; a project's folder that does not answer refused in time, holding up no other call of the space, and its late answer writing nothing

Folders at the command line: tasks add and tasks set give a task its folder with --folder, a folder relative to the working one, folder= and --here, and --clear folder takes it away; --here beside --folder is a usage error; tasks area create --folder --create makes a folder that is not there and binds it, one undo takes the project, its new area and its folder back and leaves the folder on disk; --folder . --create binds an existing folder; a refused call removes the folder --create made; tasks area list and tasks show print the folders; the old --place and place= name --folder

The agent's folder fields through the request path: a task added with folder cwd from a project's subfolder lands in the deepest project whose folder holds it with its own folder, from the project's folder itself takes the project's, from outside every project has no project and its folder, from an archived project's folder has no project, its folder and a warning; a draft that names its group keeps it; a follow-up with folder cwd; a retry replays after the folder went; organize creates a project with its folder, sets it to cwd, lists and clears it, and answers exists with the project that has a folder; cwd without a working folder, a missing folder and the old place field are refused with their reason and the field to use; has:folder and folder: in search; a group an earlier draft makes known by its slug; a refusal's op counting the call's own operations; update_task's folder from cwd

organize's writes through the request path: create a project in a new area, create of what exists answers no_change, create of a name close to another's or of a project another area has makes it while an area named to hold it keeps the typo check, rename keeping the ID with a retry that replays after the rename took the old name, move a project to another area, an area that moves nowhere, archive and unarchive with archive twice no change, and an unknown name not_found

On the 0.2 fixture migrated to 0.3, a task's run written through the write path is detached from its task as entity redaction detaches it (task and request set to null): the space stays intact with no foreign key broken, the detached run reads and still settles through the writer, and the runs table refuses a run with both a task and a routine

The installed-build migration failure and restore drill with the real 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4: a populated 0.1 fixture space, a fault planted in its migration's last step, the space left at 0.1 and served read-only with A1's message and refusing word search with why while filters answer, a restore of the pre-migration backup with the fixture's counts and last_seq; with the fault gone the same build does not try again by itself and writes no barrier backup, the build's CLI takes --retry-migration and a script's retry is refused, and the person's retry upgrades the space, whose new task tasks find finds by a word

The search tables are written in the commit: each document holds A1 3.12's fields, a commit that changes no indexed text leaves its documents and seqs alone, a tombstone removes a task's documents and its children's and a restore brings them back, an undo and a redo write the documents their inversions reach, a space without the tables writes as before, and under random writes, tombstones, restores, entity and text redactions, learnings and area renames the index equals a fresh rebuild with no stray text and passes the FTS integrity check

Pages by frozen IDs return one entry per ID, in order: the current row, a tombstoned task or deleted learning as a deleted placeholder with its reference, an ID without a row as a redacted placeholder, neither with content, and a result that lost an entry is refused

Restore into a new folder verifies sizes, SHA-256, integrity_check, revision and the sidecar's facts before the folder appears; a tampered, mismatched, linked or newer backup is refused and leaves nothing

The search index is derived: a backup made before schema 0.4, one made after it, one whose search tables are missing and one whose search tables differ each verify by a trial restore and restore into a new folder and in place, with the index made again from the copy's tasks and a new space's schema
A space whose search index alone is damaged still backs up and its backup restores whole; a writer's open makes the index again from the tasks, and leaves a sound one as it is

A backup restored into a new folder is a read-only copy until claimed: a writer is refused with SPACE_READ_ONLY_COPY, a reader reads, the mark lives in the database so a copy of the folder or the database and a missing or damaged space.json keep it, and a claim gives a new epoch and incarnation in one commit and leaves the original untouched
Restore in place, recovery and the claim of a read-only copy hold the space's claim in the process: each is refused while the space's writer is open, and no writer opens while one runs
Restore in place moves the old folder aside and keeps it, and claims the restored copy with a new epoch above every known one and a new incarnation; two claims of one backup make two incarnations

A crash at each point of a restore in place leaves the old space, the claimed new one, or a missing space that finishInterruptedRestore completes; never an unclaimed or half-built space under the space's name

A space refused with SPACE_NEEDS_RECOVERY recovers from a copy whose rollback journal SQLite played back, keeping the original folder; the copy is judged as open judges a writer, so space.json's gates stay; a copy that does not verify or is refused changes nothing, and a restore from a backup still works
